_meta.description: Plainly's health & insurance pack. Plain-English meanings for the jargon on insurance, patient-portal, and pharmacy sites. Not medical or insurance advice; check with your provider or plan for specifics.

premium.simple: the amount you pay for coverage each month
premium.detailed: Your regular payment to keep an insurance plan active — owed whether or not you use any care.

deductible.simple: what you pay yourself before insurance starts helping
deductible.detailed: The amount you cover out of pocket each year before your plan begins paying its share.
deductible.why: A lower premium often comes with a higher deductible, so you pay more when you actually need care.

copay.simple: a fixed fee you pay for a visit or prescription
copay.detailed: A set dollar amount (like $25 for a doctor visit) you pay at the time of care; insurance covers the rest.

coinsurance.simple: your percentage share of a cost after the deductible
coinsurance.detailed: Once you've met your deductible, you pay a percentage (say 20%) and insurance pays the rest.

out-of-pocket maximum.simple: the most you'll pay in a year before insurance covers everything
out-of-pocket maximum.detailed: A yearly cap on your own spending; after you hit it, the plan pays 100% of covered care.
out-of-pocket maximum.why: It's your worst-case cost for the year — worth knowing before a big treatment.

out-of-pocket.simple: costs you pay yourself, not the insurer

in-network.simple: doctors and hospitals your plan has cheaper deals with
in-network.detailed: Providers your insurance has contracted with, so you pay less. Staying in-network is usually much cheaper.

out-of-network.simple: providers your plan hasn't contracted with — usually costs more
out-of-network.detailed: Care from a doctor or facility outside your plan's network; you often pay a bigger share, sometimes the full bill.
out-of-network.why: Out-of-network care can lead to surprise bills.

explanation of benefits.simple: a summary of what insurance paid and what you owe
explanation of benefits.detailed: An EOB is not a bill — it's a statement showing how a claim was processed: the charge, what the plan covered, and your share.

claim.simple: a request to your insurer to pay for care you received
claim.detailed: The bill your provider (or you) sends to insurance so it pays its share.

prior authorization.simple: insurance approval you need before certain care is covered
prior authorization.detailed: For some treatments or drugs, the plan must sign off first, or it won't pay. It can cause delays.
prior authorization.why: Skipping required prior authorization can leave you with the full bill.

referral.simple: your main doctor's OK to see a specialist
referral.detailed: Some plans require your primary doctor to refer you before they'll cover a specialist visit.

formulary.simple: the list of drugs your plan will help pay for
formulary.detailed: Each plan covers specific medications, often in price tiers. Drugs off the list cost more or aren't covered.

generic.simple: a cheaper drug with the same active ingredient as the brand
generic.detailed: A copy of a brand-name medication that works the same way but usually costs much less.

primary care physician.detailed: The doctor you see first for most needs, who coordinates your care and referrals.

provider.simple: any doctor, clinic, or professional who gives you care

specialist.simple: a doctor focused on one area of medicine
specialist.detailed: A physician with deep training in a specific field (like a cardiologist or dermatologist), usually seen by referral.

hmo.simple: a lower-cost plan that keeps you in-network and needs referrals
hmo.detailed: Health Maintenance Organization — cheaper premiums, but you must use in-network providers and get referrals for specialists.

ppo.simple: a flexible plan that lets you see more providers without referrals
ppo.detailed: Preferred Provider Organization — more freedom to pick doctors and skip referrals, usually for a higher premium.

hsa.simple: a tax-free savings account for medical costs
hsa.detailed: Health Savings Account — money you set aside pre-tax for healthcare, paired with a high-deductible plan. Unused funds roll over.

fsa.simple: a tax-free account for medical costs that resets yearly
fsa.detailed: Flexible Spending Account — pre-tax money for healthcare, but you usually must spend it within the year or lose it.

balance billing.simple: being billed for the gap between the charge and what insurance paid
balance billing.detailed: When an out-of-network provider bills you for the leftover amount insurance didn't cover — sometimes a surprise bill.

allowed amount.simple: the price your insurer agrees a service is worth
allowed amount.detailed: The maximum your plan will count toward a covered service; your share is based on this, not the sticker price.

preventive care.simple: routine check-ups and screenings, often fully covered
preventive care.detailed: Care that keeps you healthy — annual physicals, vaccines, screenings — which many plans cover at no cost to you.

telehealth.simple: seeing a doctor by video or phone instead of in person

prescription.simple: a doctor's order for a specific medication

refill.simple: getting another supply of a medication you already have

dosage.simple: how much medicine to take and how often

open enrollment.simple: the yearly window to pick or change your health plan
open enrollment.detailed: The set period each year when you can sign up for or switch insurance; outside it you usually need a special reason.

hipaa.simple: the law that keeps your health information private
hipaa.detailed: HIPAA sets rules for how providers and insurers protect and share your medical records.

patient portal.simple: the website where you view your records and message your doctor
patient portal.detailed: A secure site or app to see test results, book visits, request refills, and contact your care team.

electronic health record.detailed: An EHR (or EMR) is the digital record of your health history that providers use and share.

diagnosis.simple: the name a doctor gives to what's wrong
